chapter_scope: v03-c09 and v03-c10 only; remaining two Volume 3 chapters and its full assessment/project package remain unfinished
review_type: Author analytic, numerical, source and instructional review; not independent certification

reviewed.reasoning: Reviewed proper-prior joint/marginal/posterior construction, support and evidence conditions, conditional versus independent sequential likelihoods, beta endpoint integrability, integration-by-parts normalization and all-positive-shape moment recurrences, count versus ordered-sequence evidence, posterior-mean consistency and normal square completion/precision units. Audited gamma shape/rate definition, normalization/moment recurrence, exposure-based likelihood and predictive zero-count integration. Reviewed credible-set interpretation and explicit fixed-parameter coverage counterexample/prior-averaged tower identity; posterior predictive integration, beta-binomial normalization and dependence/total variance, normal new-observation/new-mean laws. Audited posterior-loss/Bayes-risk implication with proper prior/measurable attained rule/finite loss, squared and absolute-loss minimizers, asymmetric binary costs and MAP/exact-point caveat; proper-prior model evidence and transformation/support/sensitivity limits. Reviewed full finite expected-utility construction from complete/transitive/continuous/independent preferences: consequence bounds, strict binary ordering, connected closed preference sections, finite indifferent replacement/reduction and affine uniqueness. Audited Jensen/concavity equivalence, combined-payoff diversification, certainty-equivalent existence/domain, insurance-price/loading distinctions and nontranslation-invariant purchase-price caveat. Reviewed bounded-small-risk Taylor/inverse proof, curvature-comparison derivative, CARA/CRRA units and domains, Gaussian exponential-square calculation, constrained exposure optima and static Ellsberg/maxmin probability comparisons.
reviewed.arithmetic: Exhaustive latent-parameter/observation sequences and asymmetric-loss values; exact rational beta-integral polynomial expansion independent of factorial recurrence, density quadrature/moments, posterior polynomial/quantiles, prior-sensitive dollar benefits, integrated beta-binomial states and conditional covariance. Checked credible-set mass and one-observation fixed-parameter coverage, posterior-loss objectives, direct prior-times-full-likelihood normal integrations under contrasting priors and normal predictive convolution. Gamma normalization/moment quadrature, count predictive integrations and exact tail-small negative-binomial series; proper-prior Bayes factors/model odds and transformed-prior CDF. Recomputed affine/nonlinear utility orderings, insurance expected wealth/certainty equivalents/loadings, log/discrete-CARA certainty equivalents, independent finite-difference CRRA curvature, small-risk convergence, exponential-normal integrals, exact-fraction exposure optima, equal-mean/variance exponential counterexample and static ambiguity-set endpoints/symmetric Bayesian ties.
reviewed.solutions: Solved all sixteen exercise prompts, checked determinate results and their probability/currency/time units, and verified prior/sample versus posterior shapes, medians/modes, future covariance, count exposure, alternative-prior shifts and cost thresholds. Open critiques have explicit data-use, support, design/causality, sensitivity, domain and loss criteria. Insurance maximum premium includes expected loss and risk loading; the gain certainty-equivalent cost shortcut is explicitly limited to CARA in the purchase exercise.
reviewed.instruction: Finite Bayes tables and joint/conditional-density concepts precede conjugate kernels and predictive mixtures. The beta and gamma integrals and normal square are derived, not only listed. Credible probability and confidence coverage receive a concrete counterexample. Loss separates belief from action. Finite-lottery preference axioms and their constructive representation are fully explained before curvature, certainty equivalents and local/exact risk formulas. All eight exercises per chapter use methods taught in their chapter or documented prerequisites. No general dynamic ambiguity, hierarchical posterior-computation or asymptotic Bayesian theorem is claimed proved here.
reviewed.sources: Retrieved official MIT beta/normal conjugacy and prediction readings, Berkeley's author-course Bayes-decision reader, NIST gamma density/integral/moments and official MIT risk/expected-utility/ambiguity chapter notes. Catalogue uses exact checked URLs and inspection scopes. Berkeley's displayed beta normalization has an inverted factor; manuscript normalization is independently derived and checked against integral/polynomial/factorial methods. Classical mathematical results are attributed as further-study methods; prose, synthetic examples, numerical laws and exercise packages are original.
reviewed.structure: Two worked examples and eight complete solved exercises per chapter, explicit prior/likelihood/utility/domain/exposure assumptions, normalization and finiteness conditions, teach-back/delayed checks and primary-source routes. Previous inference chapter now links to the available Bayesian chapter; Chapter 10's still-planned successor links to its curriculum specification. Integrated structural/source/link/anchor and numerical checks required before acceptance.

corrections: Used the independently derived beta integral normalizer instead of a reversed factor in a reference display; recorded that source limitation in its catalogue entry.
Tightened certainty-equivalent existence to compact support within the utility domain, since bounded wealth alone need not bound utility near an excluded endpoint.
Changed the urn description to a stipulated preference pattern rather than implying a newly supported claim about behavioral prevalence.
Updated the previous chapter's planned Bayesian successor route to the actual manuscript while preserving other planned-material labels.
limitations: No independent human reviewer or learner trial.
Finite numeric checks illustrate but do not prove the general representation, risk comparison or Bayes-risk theorems; their written derivations and assumptions were audited separately.
The representation proof is for a finite consequence set. Extensions to infinite outcome spaces need additional regularity and are not silently claimed.
Small-risk expansion assumes bounded centered risk, C2 utility and positive derivative; exact mean–variance certainty equivalents use CARA-normal assumptions.
The ambiguity model is a static specified-law-set example, not a general dynamic robustness theorem or empirical prevalence finding.
Example laws, observations, costs and preferences are synthetic assumptions, not observed October market/customer data or universal investment advice.
Visual/mobile/print UI QA remains pending after the earlier browser-policy rejection.
acceptance: Accepted by the author after analytic, source, complete-solution and integrated structural/numerical review. Remaining Volume 3 manuscripts/package and the Chapter 12 formal-foundations/strong-law follow-up, external learner evaluation and visual/mobile/print UI QA remain outstanding.
